title: Google Health won’t let users manually add rests between workout sets
summary: The Health Coach can do something the manual workout builder can't.
body: TL;DR Google Health’s manual workout builder lacks the option to schedule rests between sets, even though the Premium-exclusive Health Coach supports it. Live workout metrics can also fail to appear in the app, even with an active smartwatch connection. We’ve reached out to Google to find out whether fixes are in the works and when users can expect them. One of the biggest fitness upgrades in the November Pixel Drop lets Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 owners follow workouts directly on their wrists, with timers and audio cues that tell them when to move on to the next set or exercise. But as more users get access to step-by-step workouts , a scheduling limitation for rest between sets and a bug affecting live workout metrics are taking some of the shine off the experience. Multiple Google Health users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 , 3 ) report that while they can schedule rest periods between different exercises when building a custom workout, they can’t do the same between sets of an individual exercise.

title: Oura is dropping Android 11 support in December, and users risk losing health data
summary: Upgrading after the deadline won't bring back your health history.
body: TL;DR Oura will officially drop support for Android 11 on December 8, 2026. Users who don’t upgrade to Android 12 or newer by the deadline risk losing their historical health data. Those who remain on Android 11 may retain access to some limited historical app features. One of the biggest benefits of wearing an Oura Ring is that the longer you use it, the more you learn about your health. From personalized annual health recaps to long-term blood pressure trends, many of Oura’s features become more useful as you build up months or even years of health data. However, some Android users could soon lose access to that history simply because of the phone they use. Oura has updated its Android software updates support page to reveal that it will discontinue support for Android 11 on December 8, 2026. Starting on that date, you’ll need a phone running Android 12 or newer to continue enjoying the full Oura app experience.

title: Samsung is bringing Galaxy Watch 9 health features to older Galaxy Watches
summary: Even Galaxy Watch 4 owners aren't being left behind.
body: TL;DR Samsung is bringing six Galaxy Watch 9 health and fitness features to the Galaxy Watch 8 series. The upgrades include Heart Health Score, Vitals, Daily Cardio Load, Fitness Index, improved Sleep Coaching, and enhanced sleep apnea detection. Select features also support older models, with improved Sleep Coaching extending back to the Galaxy Watch 4. Samsung could break its tradition of launching a new Galaxy Watch every year as early as 2027, reportedly shifting its focus to software updates and new health features for existing smartwatches. We’re already seeing what that approach could mean for Galaxy Watch owners, as Samsung has confirmed that several health and fitness features from the Galaxy Watch 9 are making their way to last year’s models. The company began rolling out stable One UI 9 Watch to the Galaxy Watch 8 series in mid-November, with US users receiving the update shortly after. In a new announcement , Samsung has detailed six health and fitness upgrades originally introduced with the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 that are coming to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic.
